findings.summary: ROOT CAUSE OF THE EMPTY ROUND-2 SNAPSHOT now identified (previously only 'an empty round-2 snapshot' was known from INTEL_LEDGER): the Reproducer worked in its own lineage workspace /tmp/spider_intel_repro_r2 (continuing round-1 commit 1e51a5c) and committed the complete RF1/RF2 documentary fix set there as commit 0a1b3ef on DETACHED HEAD (~23 files per its own final report). The workflow's persist step then force-pushed from the MOUNTED workspace (/tmp/spider_intel_repro), which still sat at base 0a55649, so branch cycle/intel/32796176172/repro == lab/intel base with an identical tree. Net effect: ~40 minutes of completed repair delivery silently vanished; a first commit attempt also failed earlier with 'fatal: empty ident name' before git identity was configured.

The independent auditor caught the loss instead of certifying it — the key control that worked. It proved empty-snapshot identity (run_tip == origin tip == base 0a55649, same tree hash), ruled out hidden output (full filesystem walk, stash, reflog), ruled out displaced work (repo-wide git log --all over all Intel paths + ls-remote: newest Intel content anywhere remained round-1 1e51a5c / audit 099c677), explained why the `if: always()` + `commit || true` + force-push persist pattern publishes an unchanged tree when the agent's work lands elsewhere, extracted 1e51a5c from history and re-verified its manifest 18/18 OK (twice-recomputed PROOF OF CONCEPT evidence fully recoverable). Verdict REVISE (not PASS — nothing to integrate; not BLOCKED — repair needs no new evidence) with RF-A restore 1e51a5c byte-exact, RF-B/RF-C apply the two documentary fixes, RF-D add round provenance, RF-E verify delivery so an empty push cannot recur silently; round status INCONCLUSIVE with mechanism status VALIDATED_USEFUL explicitly preserved. Escalation rule stated: a second consecutive empty/unverifiable snapshot becomes BLOCKED on infrastructure grounds.

Content of the LOST commit 0a1b3ef survives only as log narrative here (LOG_ONLY): RF1 constant-dummy clause withdrawn as evidence with auditor-approved stable-controls wording adopted verbatim (wrong-context-summary fusion = 24/74 and summary-only = 24/74 re-reproduced this round via own-embedder reranking); RF2 cost footnote restated artifact-exactly as ≈12–13 would-be LLM calls (11 unique collection-side states via summarizer_cache keys with eval pass 49 hits/0 misses, plus exactly 2 conversion run-counter misses against a conversion cache holding 10 keys / 1 novel; exact attribution declared unreconcilable at artifact level; no ranking/success/novelty impact); prereg erratum appendices below frozen text; cycle1_repair2_SHA256SUMS.txt; selftest rerun 7/7 PASS. All of it is documentary-only and was successfully re-delivered in repair round 3 per accepted ledger history (PASS run 32800296360, integration fca0acb).

~64m total wall clock: scout 7s, reproducer 40m20s (largely WASTED — delivery lost; 5 provider-outage retries across 7 OpenCode attempts early in the job), auditor 23m17s spent almost entirely on loss forensics rather than science. The incident cost one full extra repair round (run 32800296360) before PASS.

failure_signatures: DETONATED_HEAD_DELIVERY_MISMATCH: agent commits on detached HEAD in a private lineage workspace while the workflow persists from a different mounted workspace → force-push publishes an unchanged base tree with exit-code success on every step; undetectable without an explicit run_tip != base assertion.
PERSIST_PUSHES_EMPTY_TREE_ON_NO_OUTPUT: `if: always()` + `commit || true` + force-push patterns convert silent production failure into a valid-looking but empty published snapshot.
research_opportunities: Adopt the auditor's RF-E pattern as standard lane plumbing: after each persist, assert pushed tip != base and (for repairs) that required paths exist in the pushed tree; treat violation as immediate job failure. This is the cheapest structural prevention of repeat empty-snapshot incidents across all lanes.
Second-consecutive-empty-snapshot ⇒ BLOCKED escalation (stated by this audit) is a reusable termination rule for repair loops anywhere.
